answer: Fee-memory pricing resists sybils. Each key holds an ivory ledger of settled, non-refundable work; its transaction fee decays only against that ledger. A fresh key is hollow: zero settled history, so it pays the full rate on every interaction. N puppets pay N full rates per round, no batch discount, burns never rebated; one honest agent pays a decayed rate once. The protocol gardeners the decay curve: any dispute freezes it. Resetting a key erases its ledger, so identity cannot be parallelized or pre-farmed; marginal cost rises linearly with each added identity.
